newsitem.title: USA: Calif. courts could be forced to make cuts -report.
newsitem.headline: Calif. courts could be forced to make cuts -report.

text.p: California trial courts could be forced to reduce their budgets by up to $90 million because the state Legislature failed to enact a court funding measure, according to a state report.
The legislation, which would have increased certain court filing fees to generate about $90 million in new revenues, failed passage in the Legislature earlier this year.
As a result, the trial courts will have to reduce their budgets by up to $90 million or counties will have to make up the difference, the state's Legislative Analyst said.

The legislation, Assembly Bill 2553, would have consolidated the costs of operations of the trial courts at the state level. Under the legislation, the county contribution for trial court funding would have been capped and the state would have become responsible for funding all future cost increases for trial courts.

"As a result of the failure of AB 2553, the Legislature will be under pressure -- especially from trial courts and counties -- to enact legislation early in the new legislative session to make technical adjustments to the budget act appropriation for the trial court funding program," the Legislative Analyst said in the report.
